title: Adaptive multiphasic reservation for continuous batcher on mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Production traffic mixes short prompts (single-turn user queries) and long multi-turn responses (generated content, code completions). The existing continuous batcher treats slot reservation and KV cache residency conservatively which causes two problems: (1) long responses occupy GPU KV slabs for extended periods, preventing short-turn requests from being coalesced and increasing p99 latency; (2) naive eviction policies lead to repeated cold starts for popular short-context dialogs, increasing token cost.

Goal: Tune the continuous batching scheduler and KV residency policy to improve p50/p95 token latency for short-turn requests while preserving throughput for long responses and maintaining <=2% regression on token cost. We aim for measurable improvements in p95 latency for short prompts (target -20%) and stable GPU memory utilization across peak windows.
proposed_solution: Introduce a multiphasic reservation strategy: small-time-window preferential reservation for short-turn candidates (heuristic: prompt length <= 64 tokens or recent short-turn history) and adaptive spill/compaction for long responses. Implement a predictor-based micro-horizon that estimates remaining generated tokens per request using prefix features, and use that to dynamically shrink or expand KV reservation. Combine with a conservative "evict-on-insert" policy that prefers removing least-recently-prefetched long-response segments first. Add a GPU-slab-aware compaction pass triggered when fragmentation exceeds threshold. All changes behind runtime feature flag 'mp-reserve-v1'.
experiments: A/B: route 10% of production traffic to mp-reserve-v1 on one 8xA100 cluster (canary).
Offline: replay mixed traffic from 2026-02 logs into simulator with exact-GPU-slab model to validate fragmentation and eviction behavior.
Microbench: synthetic short-heavy and long-heavy workloads to quantify latency/cost tradeoffs and tail behavior.
metrics: eviction_rate.long_segments - track absolute and relative change
acceptance_criteria: Canary cluster shows p95 short_turn reduction >= 15% without >3% increase in overall token cost.
No increase in observed OOM incidents; gpu_mem_frag_ratio stays within target during peak windows.
Rollout automation (feature flag gating + per-cluster thresholds) implemented and documented.
Unit/integration tests for predictor, reservation controller, and compaction pass included + benchmark reproducibility in CI harness.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: merge behind feature flag, smoke tests in integration staging. Stage 1 (canary): 10% traffic on one cluster for 72h. Monitor latency, cost, OOM, fragmentation. Stage 2: widen to 30% after 1-week steady canary with automated rollback on threshold breaches. Stage 3: global rollout per-region with gradual ramp and telemetry gating. Backout path: disable 'mp-reserve-v1' flag and revert compaction trigger if regressions exceed thresholds.
risks: Predictor misestimates long responses and causes premature eviction leading to repeated KV reloads and cost spikes.
Compaction pass increases CPU/GPU sync points and temporarily raises latency if triggered too aggressively.
Edge cases: multi-session dialogs with alternating short/long turns may oscillate reservation, causing ping-pong eviction behavior.
